title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, Status Page & Customer Comms
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:

This playbook documents Redwood Inference's standardized on-call and incident response process. It covers alerting and triage, role responsibilities, runbook patterns, postmortem expectations, on-call rotations, game day guidance, status page templates and customer communications. Use this page as the canonical source for runbook structure and templates; individual services must link their service-specific runbooks and contact lists.

Goals and scope:
- Ensure fast, consistent triage and mitigation for production incidents affecting API, Dedicated, Private deployment, and Console surfaces.
- Minimize user impact and restore best-effort availability while preserving data integrity and security.
- Produce high-quality postmortems and actionable remediation to reduce recurrence.

Service coverage and SLOs (examples):
- redwood-api-gen (hosted API): Availability SLO 99.9% regionally; API p95 latency < 300ms for text-generation; error rate < 0.1% by request count.
- redwood-dedicated-proxy: Throughput SLOs per reserved pool; tail-latency p99 < 2s for synchronous requests.
- embeddings-service: Batch/streaming SLO p95 latency < 150ms.

1) Incident detection and alerting
- Alerts originate from: Prometheus Alertmanager metrics, Datadog monitors, synthetic checks (k6/uptime checks), health endpoints, customer-reported tickets (Zendesk), or automated Canary failures.
- Alert routing rules (high-level):
  - Severity P0 (customer-facing outage / data loss): page primary SRE, notify eng-oncall channel, SMS & PagerDuty escalation.
  - Severity P1 (degraded primary functionality / high error rates): page primary on-call, notify Slack #incidents and product PM.
  - Severity P2 (minor degradation / non-critical errors): create ticket, page secondary if unresolved >30m.
- Detection thresholds (examples):
  - error_rate_30s > 0.5% and sustained for 3 minutes -> P1 alert
  - 5 failed canary runs in 10 minutes -> P0 alert
  - API availability < 99.5% over 15m -> P0

2) Roles & responsibilities (incident roles)
- Incident Commander (IC): owns coordination, public comms cadence, mitigation decisions, and postmortem writeup. Typically the primary SRE or senior on-call.
- Primary on-call (Responder): performs immediate triage, executes runbook actions, escalates to IC if scope grows.
- Secondary on-call (Backup): supports escalation, takes over paging if primary is unavailable.
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): owners of affected services (e.g., runtime, networking, gpu-fleet) who provide technical fixes.
- Communications Lead: writes status page updates and external customer comms. Usually product or incident IC.
- Exec & Legal Notifier: alerted on P0 incidents; coordinates regulatory/customer notification where required.

Escalation matrix (timings):
1. Pager -> primary on-call (immediate).
2. No ack in 60s -> notify secondary.
3. No progress in 5 minutes for P0 -> escalate to IC & notify execs.
4. If on-call cannot resolve within 15 minutes for P0 -> initiate failover/rollback runbook.

3) Triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
1. Confirm alert: check Prometheus / Datadog graphs (error rates, latency, traffic).
2. Validate scope: which regions/tenants/customers are affected? Identify customer-reported tickets.
3. Identify recent changes: deploys in last 60 minutes (CI/CD), config changes, infra events.
4. Collect evidence: logs (ELK/CloudWatch), recent core dumps, kernel/driver messages, GPU telemetry.
5. Run quick mitigations: route traffic away from region, scale replicas, enable degraded-mode features, or apply circuit-breaker.
6. Assign incident severity and name (YYYYMMDD-Service-ShortDescription).
7. Notify #incidents channel and create incident doc in Confluence (link template below).

4) Runbook structure and example steps
- Runbook naming: service-runbook-version.json or service-runbook-{major}.md. Include owner, pagerduty escalation key, runbook tested date.
- Required runbook fields: owner, primary contact, runbook steps, quick checks, rollback steps, mitigation, post-incident actions.

Example: redwood-api-gen runbook (shortened)
- Quick checks:
  - curl -sSf https://redwood-api-gen.prod.region.example.com/health | jq .status
  - kubectl get pods -n redwood-api | grep CrashLoopBackOff
  - datadog monitor show api-error-rate-12345
- Immediate mitigations:
  1) If pods OOM or CrashLoopBackOff, restart deployment: kubectl rollout restart deploy/redwood-api --namespace=redwood-api
  2) If error rate due to model-serving timeouts, toggle fallback model: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' https://controlplane.example.com/v1/services/redwood-api/config -d '{"model_fallback":true}'
  3) Increase replicas for redwood-api-deployment: kubectl scale deploy/redwood-api --replicas=10 -n redwood-api
- Rollback procedure (CI/CD):
  - Identify offending revision: ci status list --service redwood-api --since 1h
  - Roll back to last known-good: ci deploy rollback --service redwood-api --revision <REV>

5) Communication templates (status page & customer comms)
- Status page updates (use Statuspage / status.redwood.com):
  - Initial (within 15 minutes):
    Title: [Investigating] Service degradation for redwood-api-gen (region)
    Body: We are investigating increased error rates and elevated latencies for the hosted text-generation API in region <region>. Customers may see 5xx errors or timeouts. Our on-call team is actively investigating. Impact: degraded API responses for a subset of requests. Next update: in 30 minutes or when we have new information.
  - Update (every 30 minutes or at major milestone):
    - What changed since last update, scope, mitigation steps taken, estimated time to resolution (if known).
  - Resolved:
    Title: [Resolved] Service restored for redwood-api-gen (region)
    Body: Service availability has been restored. Root cause: <short summary>. Next steps and mitigations: <link to postmortem>.

- Customer email template (for P0 / multi-customer incidents):
  Subject: Service incident affecting Redwood Inference API — update
  Body: Hello <CustomerName>, we wanted to inform you of an incident that affected the Redwood Inference API on <date/time> that may have impacted requests to <service>. We detected increased error rates and latency between <start> and <end>. Our team mitigated the issue by <short mitigation>. We will follow up with a full postmortem and any recommended actions. Contact: support@redwood.example.com.

6) Postmortem template and expectations
- Publish within 72 hours (draft) and final postmortem within 7 business days for P0/P1 incidents.
- Required sections in the Confluence postmortem doc:
  - Title: Incident YYYYMMDD — <Service> — <Short description>
  - Summary: 2-3 sentence customer-facing summary.
  - Impact: affected customers/regions, duration, and business impact estimate.
  - Timeline: bullet timeline with timestamps and actors (detection -> mitigation -> resolution).
  - Root cause analysis: technical root cause with evidence and why detection/prevention failed.
  - Corrective actions: list of action items with owners and ETA.
  - Preventative measures: changes to monitoring, runbooks, or architecture.
  - Postmortem review attendees, lessons learned, and follow-ups.

Postmortem example snippet:
- Timeline:
  - 2026-01-12T10:03Z — Synthetic canary failed (5 runs) -> PagerDuty P0 triggered to SRE-primary.
  - 2026-01-12T10:05Z — IC declared incident, scaled redwood-api replicas and enabled fallback.
  - 2026-01-12T10:20Z — Error rate dropped below threshold, traffic restored via region routing.
- Root cause: memory leak in model-loading path when concurrent warmups & GPU contention triggered OOMs on 2 nodes.
- Actions:
  - Fix: patch model loader to limit concurrent warmups (owner: Runtime, ETA: 2026-02-01).
  - Monitoring: add gauge for model-loader concurrent warmups and alert at 80% of node memory (owner: Observability, ETA: 2026-01-20).

7) On-call rotations & handoffs
- Rotation model: 1-week primary on-call (week starts Monday 09:00 UTC), 1-week secondary on-call paired with primary.
- Paging schedule: primary is first responder; secondary receives escalations and takes over if primary is offline.
- Handoff checklist (end of shift):
  1) Summarize open incidents and mitigation status.
  2) Confirm follow-ups and outstanding action items.
  3) Share any ongoing experiments or rollouts that could affect availability.
  4) Update the on-call calendar (Google Calendar) and Slack status to reflect coverage.
- On-call responsibilities:
  - Monitor for alerts and respond within the escalation windows.
  - Keep runbooks up-to-date; add playbook-tested date to the top of each runbook.
  - Participate in at least one game day per quarter.

8) Game days (exercise guide)
- Purpose: validate runbooks, verify failover paths, measure detection-to-mitigation time, and surface gaps in instrumentation.
- Frequency: quarterly per major service (API, runtime, gpu-fleet, control-plane).
- Typical scenarios:
  - Canary failure & multi-region traffic shift.
  - GPU node flapping in Dedicated pool and scheduler overload.
  - Control-plane DB latency spike causing config propagation delays.
- Game day run (example agenda):
  09:00 — Kickoff & read scenario (roles assigned).
  09:10 — Inject failure (synthetic canary failures or simulated node drain).
  09:30 — Triage and mitigation window.
  10:15 — Restore & verification.
  10:45 — Retrospective & action item assignment.

9) Connecting to status & post-incident processes
- Maintain Statuspage components: redwood-api, control-plane, dedicated-proxy, embeddings-service. Keep component owners current.
- After any P0/P1 incident:
  1) IC creates a post-incident Confluence page using the postmortem template.
  2) Assign action items with concrete owners and ETA, track in Jira.
  3) Schedule a postmortem readout within 5 business days.

10) Templates (copyable snippets)
- Incident doc starter (Confluence page title): Incident YYYYMMDD — <Service> — <Short description>
- Initial Slack post (use #incidents): @here Incident declared for <service>: <short description>. Incident doc: <link>. IC: <name>. Primary: <name>. Please pause non-urgent deploys.
- Statuspage initial (see section 5)
- Customer email (see section 5)

Appendix A — Useful commands and checks
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-api -o wide
- kubectl logs $(kubectl get pod -n redwood-api -o name | head -n1) -n redwood-api --since=10m
- curl -sS https://redwood-api-gen.prod.region.example.com/health | jq .
- datadog monitors search "api-error-rate" --from "15m"
- pd incident create --service "redwood-api" --summary "P0: API outage"

Appendix B — Ownership matrix (examples)
- redwood-api-gen: Owner: Runtime team (runtime-owners@redwood.example.com)
- gpu-fleet: Owner: infra/gpu-fleet team (gpu-fleet@redwood.example.com)
- control-plane: Owner: eng-platform (platform-owners@redwood.example.com)

Appendix C — Runbook testing & maintenance policy
- Each on-call rotation must test at least one critical runbook per week (smoke test).
- Runbooks must include a "last-tested" date on the header. If a runbook is older than 90 days, mark as stale and schedule an update.

Appendix D — Regulatory & legal escalation guidance
- For incidents involving customer data exposure, notify Legal and Security within 1 hour. Use the Security incident form: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security.
- For SEV-level incidents impacting enterprise customers, follow contract notification timelines in finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process.

Document maintenance
- Owner: Engineering SRE lead (Ava Martinez).
- Review cadence: quarterly. Keep this page linked from each service's runbook and the eng-sre index.
